A league of western Mongol tribes in the Altai, western Mongolia and the upper Yenisei, strong from about 1400. The map shows it in 1492 and 1500.

After the Yuan dynasty lost China in 1368, the Mongols split into an eastern group under the heirs of Kublai and the western Oirats, and the two fought for a century. Under Esen Taishi the Oirats briefly dominated the whole steppe; in 1449, in the Tumu Crisis, they captured the Ming emperor. Esen then took the title of khan, which only Genghis's line was meant to hold, and was killed in 1455.

By 1500 the eastern Mongols under Dayan Khan had the upper hand, and the Oirats were pushed west. In the 17th century the tribes went separate ways: the Dzungars built the Dzungar Khanate, and the Torghuts moved to the Volga as the Kalmyks. In 1640 Oirat and eastern Mongol princes agreed a shared law, the Mongol and Oirat Code.
